strengths: The motivating construction clearly demonstrates why ignoring context or intervening on every controllable variable can prevent recovery of the optimal policy. This establishes a meaningful problem.

Combining causal scope reduction with contextual BO and a running-average UCB selector is a useful algorithmic design. The decomposition into scope-selection regret and within-scope optimisation regret is informative.

Experiments use 110 random seeds, report uncertainty, and include context-removal, noise, and BO-backend ablations. The constructed examples demonstrate benefits from contextual policies and reduced optimisation dimensionality.
weaknesses: The main regret proof contains unresolved errors. On page 27, the action gap f_i^*(c) − f_i(x,c) is bounded by the variation of f_i^* across contexts; this is false when the optimal value is constant across contexts but actions can be suboptimal. Consequently, the stated martingale argument is not established. Additionally, Equation (21) and the final derivation use c(T), defined using the maximum information gain gamma(T), whereas Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 claim the smaller arm-averaged information gain in the leading instance-dependent term. That strengthening is not justified.

The reduction from general mixed policies to the theoretical model needs justification. Definition 1 permits sequential scopes in which an earlier intervention changes a context used by a later intervention. Algorithm 2 instead observes all contexts before jointly selecting actions and assumes fixed, policy-independent context distributions. Section B.1 also collapses scopes using only their unions of action and context variables, discarding action-specific information restrictions. Additional structural restrictions or a sequential formulation are needed to support guarantees for the original policy class.

The evaluation does not isolate the contribution of the proposed scope-selection rule. There is no comparison that holds the POMPS set and BO backend fixed while replacing this rule with uniform allocation or another selector. Functional Causal BO is discussed but not evaluated. Most comparisons therefore establish the benefits of a richer policy class or causal dimensionality reduction, rather than the superiority of the new learning strategy.

Scalability remains unsupported. Scope enumeration is explicitly exponential, but preprocessing time, memory consumption, and scaling with the number of candidate scopes are not reported. The 86-variable example mainly adds redundant variables and retains only two POMPSs; the other experiments also have only one or two, providing little evidence about difficult scope-selection problems.

Reproducibility is incomplete despite the claimed public implementation: the manuscript provides no repository link or concrete experimental settings for the exploration schedules and GP configuration. Some benchmark equations are inconsistent: Appendix A.1.2 omits Cancer from the stated PSA equation before substituting it, and Appendix A.3 defines C4 using itself despite the acyclic graph. These discrepancies affect reconstruction of the environments and verification of their reported optima.
